To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immunostimulation function of tissue dendritic cells, but not splenic dendritic cells, is dependent on granulocyte–macro-phage colony‐stimulation‐factor.
the immunostimulation capacity of tissue dendritic cells is affected by the local environment, and that this effect is mediated by granulocyte‐macrophage colony stimulating factor.
tissue DC are affected in situ by GM‐CSF and that this affects their immunostimulatory potential, which may have important consequences for autoimmune disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GM‐CSF on DC in autoimmune diabetes.
the regulation of tissue DC function and its relevance to autoimmune disease.
the role of tissue‐derived GM‐CSF in regulating the immunostimulating function of tissue DC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tissue dendritic cell immunostimulatory potential can be modulated by GM‐CSF in situ, and the immunostimulating function of tissue dendritic cells is dependent on the local environment.

the immunostimulator function of islet cells is partially dependent on the presence of granulocyte–macrohage colony‐stimulation factor, which is present in the islets of non‐obese mice, and that the immunostimulation function of spleen cells is not dependent on the presence or absence of granulocyte‐macrophage colony‐stimulatin factor.
the immunostimulation function of islet‐derived dendritic cells is partially dependent on granulocyte– macrophage colony‐stimulation‐factor (GM-CSF).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GM‐CSF‐dependent regulation of dendritic cell function in the pancreas may be an important mechanism for controlling the development of autoimmunity.
GM‐CSF regulates the function of tissue‐associated DC, but not that of spleen‐associated DC.
tissue‐associated DC are not only involved in the regulation of immune responses in situ, but are also regulated by the tissue environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GM‐CSF is a key regulator of tissue dendritic cells.
GM‐CSF can be an important regulator of the immunostimulating function of DC.
the immunostimulation of dendritic cells is not a uniform function.
